- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or dips; reduce forecasted values by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days post-spike.
- After a significant upward spike (e.g., >80), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — cap forecasted values at +10% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence — apply smoothing filter or use 10-day moving average for forecast calibration.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it — add a 3-day lag correction: if true value drops >5% from peak, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to “late correction” — if true outcome shows a sharp drop in last 3 days, model often misses it; adjust forecast to match last 3-day trend if sentiment is neutral or negative.
